content: Erythromycin stearate can increase the levels or effects of ivacaftor by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. If co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, the ivacaftor dose should be reduced. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage modifications. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Erythromycin stearate also increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate ivosidenib plasma concentrations, increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. Alternative therapies should be considered, as both ivosidenib and erythromycin stearate can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid combining QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib, or replace them with alternative treatments. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should not be co-administered with ivosidenib unless unavoidable, in which case patients should be monitored for loss of therapeutic effects. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so alternative therapies are recommended.
